title: Existence of the normalized degree-one character deletion cochain map
statement: Let $A$ be a commutative condensed ring, $G$ any profinite group and $D$ a resolution of [lem-sfb-condensed-internal-bar-resolution], with the sizes and internal modules of [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring, sk-def-sfb-module-objects, def-sfb-condensed-action-module, def-weil-size-convention]. Use the complex and component identifications of [def-sfb-internal-bar-character-data]. For every additive condensed character $a$ of [def-sfb-condensed-unipotent-class] there exists a cochain map $L_a:P\to P[1]$ with IsLift: its components are equivariant and, for every profinite $S$, send $[g_0,\dots,g_{n+1}]$ to $a(g_0^{-1}g_1)[g_1,\dots,g_{n+1}]$. There is no ordered iteration, augmentation comparison, or inhomogeneous cochain in this assertion.

source.place: Paragraph (3), open direct image; agent-written internal-bar expansion, extracted from lem-sfb-internal-bar-character-lifts.

proof.text: For every profinite $S$, the proposed image $a(g_0^{-1}g_1)[g_1,\ldots,g_n]$ is a section of $P_{n-1}(S)$, natural under every $T\to S$: $a$ is a condensed morphism, and the generator map and scalar multiplication commute with restriction. The free-module universal property and generator equality test of [lem-sfb-condensed-free-linearization-tensor] therefore give a unique internal $A$-linear $L_{a,n}$. For $u\in C(S,G)$, $(ug_0)^{-1}(ug_1)=g_0^{-1}g_1$, and $u$ takes the remaining generator to $[ug_1,\ldots,ug_n]$. The scalar is unchanged because the coefficient action is trivial. Thus the generator equivariance test of [lem-sfb-condensed-group-algebra-exact-forgetful] proves equivariance. Put all the other components equal to zero as stated.

Check the chain identity on generalized generators using [lem-sfb-condensed-free-linearization-tensor]. For $n\geq2$ write $a_{ij}=a(g_i^{-1}g_j)$. In $\partial_{n-1}L_{a,n}+L_{a,n-1}\partial_n$, deleting $g_i$ for $i\geq2$ gives the same tuple with coefficients $(-1)^{i-1}a_{01}$ and $(-1)^ia_{01}$, which cancel. The remaining tuple $[g_2,\ldots,g_n]$ has coefficient $a_{01}+a_{12}-a_{02}=0$, because $g_0^{-1}g_2=(g_0^{-1}g_1)(g_1^{-1}g_2)$ and $a(xy)=a(x)+a(y)$. At $n=1$ the two terms are zero since the unaugmented $d_P^0$ and $L_a^0$ are zero; at $n=0$ and in positive degrees the same holds. Thus $d_PL_a=-L_ad_P$ in every degree. As $d_{P[1]}=-d_P$, these are exactly the cochain-map equations for $P\to P[1]$.

Equality on free generators determines the transported components by lem-sfb-condensed-free-linearization-tensor. Cancel the term and shift isomorphisms to recover equality in every negative degree. At degree zero both maps are zero because their target is P^1=0; in positive degrees their source is zero. The Lean theorem deletion_unique proves this separately, and exists_unique_deletion combines it with the existence statement.
